P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Generally free. All foreign-exchange transactions take place in a private market where everyone may buy and sell foreign currency through commercial banks and exchange houses, under a floating rate (trade.gov).

sources.title: Dominican Republic Country Commercial Guide — Trade Financing
sources.quote: All foreign exchange transactions operate in the private market where all sectors of the Dominican economy are free to buy and sell foreign exchange through commercial banks and exchange houses (casas de cambio).

P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Yes. Dominican banks (e.g. Banreservas, Popular, BHD) offer dollar or euro accounts that work like a savings or current account in foreign currency, useful if you receive income in dollars (Bolsillo Práctico). The private FX market is free (see P1).

sources.quote: Cuenta en dólares (o euros) Funciona como una cuenta de ahorro o corriente, pero en moneda extranjera.

P3_local_gateways.answer: Global platform availability for Dominican Republic (automated collector snapshots, Oct 2026). L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: Anyone liable to pay taxes, including freelancers, must register in the National Taxpayer Registry (RNC) with the DGII.
L1_registration.note: Single secondary source (DR Lawyer); DGII infographic timed out (504) on 2026-10-23.

L2_tax_id.question: Tax ID: who needs one, how to get it?
L2_tax_id.answer: The RNC (Registro Nacional de Contribuyentes), administered by the DGII. For Dominican individuals, the RNC is their cédula de identidad y electoral number; legal entities and foreigners without a cédula get a 9-digit number (Siempre al Día). The DGII lets anyone look up a taxpayer by RNC or cédula (Revista Mercado). Registration is free via the DGII Oficina Virtual with form RC-01; a basic individual registration does not by itself allow issuing tax invoices (comprobantes) (search summary).

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Territorial; residents taxed on foreign investment/financial gains (after the third year for new residents). Deloitte 2026 confirms the territorial system; rates run from exempt (up to DOP 416,220) through 15% and 20% to 25%.

sources.title: Dominican Republic - Individual - Taxes on personal income
sources.quote: The Dominican Republic follows a territorial concept for the determination of taxable income.

sources.title: Dominican Republic - Individual - Taxes on personal income
sources.quote: Dominican-source income is subject to tax, while foreign-source income is generally not.

sources.title: Dominican Republic - Individual - Residence
sources.quote: Persons are resident in the Dominican Republic if they remain in the country for more than 182 days during a calendar year, whether continuously or not.

sources.title: Dominican Republic Highlights 2026
sources.quote: Basis: The Dominican Republic primarily operates a territorial system of taxation, although resident individuals are subject to tax on certain foreign-source investment income.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: VAT/sales tax: 18% (ITBIS). ITBIS registration is part of general taxpayer registration (you cannot register for VAT only), and a 0% rate applies to exports (Deloitte 2026). Deloitte 2026 confirms the 18% standard rate.

D1_id_document.question: Identity documents residents use for KYC (gateways, banks, platforms)
D1_id_document.answer: National identity card: Cédula de Identidad y Electoral (CIE)(Personality Verification Card) (Wikipedia, compulsory-ID list). If needed, an underage ID card may be obtained at the age of 16, yet the official ID (which will allow the individual to vote) is obtained at 18. Banks and payment platforms usually also accept a passport; their exact lists were not captured.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (5) Client payments by PayPal (on PayPal's Payouts list as 'Send, receive, and withdraw'). (6) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
